name: Drought
value: Sudan record-dry rains; no famine declared
summary: Sudan's driest rainy season in over three decades keeps famine risk high; El Niño threatens southern African crops
state: Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest nationally in more than three decades, with North Darfur its driest since 1984 and farmers in Gedaref expecting a fraction of last year's crop (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). In South Africa, commentary on 2 Nov said El Niño threatens the coming crop but ample maize stocks cushion the blow (Daily Maverick). Searches on 22 Nov found no new drought-driven famine declaration and no harvest failure at a major exporter, so severe drought in crop regions keeps Watch.
for_you: Drought in Sudan and an El Niño threat to southern African harvests mainly affect food prices and food security in those regions. Humanitarian appeals from WFP and FAO describe where needs are greatest.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan) = Watch; no famine or exporter harvest failure

sources.title: TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought
Daily Maverick — El Niño threatens SA's crops but ample maize stocks cushion the blow

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
